caption: Migraines don’t just happen if you get them and nothing seems to work
transcript: Migraines don't just happen if you get them and nothing seems to work. I'm about to show you one simple shift that can feel like a light switch in your head once you try it. Make sure to save this video so you can come back to it anytime. When migraines hit, it can feel like your whole world shrinks. Light becomes too bright. Sound becomes too loud. Even simple thoughts feel heavy. What most people don't realize is this. The brain isn't weak in these moments. It's overwhelmed. The nervous system is stuck in overdrive. And very often the trigger isn't lack of oxygen. It's breathing too much, too fast, without noticing. Try this. Close your mouth. Breathe slowly through your nose. Inhale for four seconds. Exhale gently for six to eight seconds. Stay here for three to five minutes. This quiet rhythm signals safety to the brain. Carbon dioxide rises just enough to relax blood vessels and soften the pressure inside the head. Many people notice the tension begin to loosen, sometimes slowly, sometimes surprisingly fast. This is not forcing relief. This is allowing the nervous system to stand down and reminding the body it no longer needs to fight. If this brought even a moment of relief, my 30-day healing journey was created for moments like this. A gentle daily practice to calm the nervous system, restore balance, and help you reconnect with your body. You'll find it through the link in my profile.
